prd.note: Decomposed on 2026-11-20 in the night run (the owner has not answered the decision review: Q-1 - Q-5 are blocked tasks). Milestone M7 "Owner tooling" (T114 - T117, no PRD; D76, D77) stays first. PRD 3 tasks are archived in ralph/archive/prd-3-roommate-matching-tasks.json.

tasks.title: Bot avatar: public/bot-avatar.png, a 512 x 512 square made from the logo (D77)
acceptance: public/bot-avatar.png exists and is committed: a 512 x 512 PNG made from public/logo.png (1536 x 1024: the rounded-square gradient mark centred on a white background) with the mark centred and the logo's background colour kept (no transparency, no new colour); made with the system `sips` tool in a one-off command, for example `sips -c 1024 1024 public/logo.png --out public/bot-avatar.png` (centre crop to the square) then `sips -z 512 512 public/bot-avatar.png`; the exact commands are named in the progress entry. sharp is not a dependency and no dependency is added

A unit test (src/lib/bot/bot-avatar.test.ts) reads the PNG header of public/bot-avatar.png without a new dependency (the PNG signature, then the IHDR width and height at bytes 16 - 23) and asserts 512 x 512, and that the file is under 200 kB; it passes for any 512 x 512 PNG, so the owner may replace the file with his own
The progress entry's Owner review says the owner may replace public/bot-avatar.png with another 512 x 512 PNG before running `npm run bot:profile` (T115)
tasks.notes:
D77 (evening of 2026-11-19). The avatar is what T115 sends with setMyProfilePhoto. If the sandbox denies `sips`, block the task with the exact commands for the owner; never add an image dependency for this.

tasks.title: Bot profile script: name, descriptions and photo through the Bot API, `npm run bot:profile -- [--dry-run]` (D77)
acceptance: src/lib/bot/profile-texts.ts holds the texts as the source of truth: BOT_PROFILE with, for the default (RU) and for language codes uk, en and pl (pl = the EN texts, D68), the name (agent draft, e.g. 'Passflat'; listed for review), the description and the short description moved verbatim from docs/marketing/bot-profile.md ('About' = short description); BOT_PROFILE_LIMITS = { name: 64, description: 512, shortDescription: 120 } (the Bot API limits), typed so every language has all three texts

src/lib/bot/profile.ts exports applyBotProfile(api, { dryRun, photoPath }) that calls api.setMyName, api.setMyDescription and api.setMyShortDescription for the default (no language_code) and for uk, en and pl, then api.setMyProfilePhoto({ photo: { type: 'static', photo: new InputFile(photoPath) } }) with public/bot-avatar.png (T114); it validates every text against BOT_PROFILE_LIMITS before the first call and throws naming the key and language on a breach; with dryRun it prints each call (method, language_code, text length or file) and makes no request; it returns the list of calls for the tests

scripts/tg-profile.ts (a thin runner in the style of scripts/tg-webhook.ts, covered by knip's scripts/** entry) is run as `npm run bot:profile -- [--dry-run]` (package.json script with the same env flags as bot:webhook: .env.local and .env); it reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from the environment only, exits 1 with a message when it is missing, never reads a file in the repository for the token, builds the grammY Bot and calls applyBotProfile; `--dry-run` works without a token too and makes no request

Tests (src/lib/bot/profile-texts.test.ts, src/lib/bot/profile.test.ts) with a fake api object: every text of every language is within 64 / 512 / 120 characters (and the test proves it fails on a 513-character description); the honesty rules of roommate-posting-kit.test.ts (brokenRules: no 'verified', no promise of a match, date or result, no figure) run over every text, with the rule list shared from one test-support module so both tests use the same list; the exact sequence of calls and their language codes (default, uk, en, pl), the pl texts equal the en texts; the photo call carries the file; dryRun makes no call; nothing in the suite calls Telegram

docs/marketing/bot-profile.md stays the human-readable copy: its header says the source of truth is src/lib/bot/profile-texts.ts and that the owner runs `npm run bot:profile` (after `--dry-run`) instead of setting the texts in BotFather; a test asserts that the Markdown's text blocks equal the module's texts so the two cannot drift (the 'bot profile texts' block of roommate-posting-kit.test.ts moves to the new test or reads the module)

Docs: src/lib/bot/README.md 'Going live' (step 1 and step 5) says the production bot's name, descriptions, short descriptions and photo are set by `npm run bot:profile` (owner only, after the token is set in the environment; `--dry-run` first), and that the dev bot @passflatdev_bot can be used to try it; docs/development-workflow.md 'Commands with additional effects' gets a `npm run bot:profile -- …` row (sets the bot profile through the Bot API; owner only; `--dry-run` has no effect); docs/specs/05-measurement-docs.md §Posting kit's bot-profile bullet says the script sets them and the Markdown is the copy
The name, descriptions and short descriptions in every language are listed in the progress entry as draft copy for the owner's review
tasks.notes: D77 (evening of 2026-11-19); D68 for pl = EN; D63 for the EN deposit line. The installed grammY 1.46 (@grammyjs/types 5.0.0) declares setMyName, setMyDescription, setMyShortDescription and setMyProfilePhoto (InputProfilePhoto). A client language without a text falls back to the default text in Telegram, which is RU, as normalizeLocale does in the bot. Checks never call Telegram; the script is an owner command with an external effect (docs/development-workflow.md).

tasks.title: One place for the production bot's username: the posting kit's `<bot>` placeholder is filled from NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME by a documented step (D76)
acceptance: The username has one place, NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME (already read by the website's bot links); nothing new stores it. src/lib/bot/bot-username.ts exports isValidBotUsername(value) (Telegram's rule: 5 - 32 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_], ending in 'bot' case-insensitively, no leading @) and fillBotPlaceholder(markdown, username), which replaces every `<bot>` (in `t.me/<bot>` links and `@<bot>` mentions) and refuses an invalid username; unit tests for both, including that the filled posting kit contains no `<bot>` and that every filled t.me link still parses with parseStartPayload to { kind: 'roommate' }

scripts/tg-posts.ts, run as `npm run bot:posts` (package.json script with the same env flags as bot:webhook), prints docs/marketing/roommate-posts.md to stdout with the placeholders filled from NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME, exits 1 with a message when the variable is missing or invalid, and writes nothing to the repository; it is the documented step the owner runs before the first slot (`NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME=<production username> npm run bot:posts > <a file outside the repo>` when .env.local holds the dev bot's username)

docs/marketing/roommate-posts.md 'How to use a template' describes that step and says the kit in the repository keeps `<bot>` on purpose (no username is committed before the owner chooses it, and the dev bot's username never lands in a post); docs/marketing/roommate-posting-log.md holds no `<bot>` (it holds none today; a test asserts it stays so); src/lib/bot/README.md 'Going live' step 5 names the variable as the one place and the step; docs/development-workflow.md 'Commands with additional effects' gets a `npm run bot:posts` row (prints only; no external effect)

A test asserts that no file under docs/marketing, src/lib/bot (texts.ts, deposit-texts.ts, roommate-texts.ts) or src/i18n/messages holds a hardcoded t.me bot link with a username (only `<bot>` or a value from the environment); test fixtures with passflat_test_bot in *.test.ts files are allowed
tasks.notes: D76 (evening of 2026-11-19): the production username is Open; T117 records it once the owner answers. The posting kit's test (roommate-posting-kit.test.ts) expects `@<bot>` in the no-link templates and parses links with `<bot>` in them: keep the placeholder in the repository and fill it only in the printed copy.

tasks.title: Set the production bot username (owner question, D76)
acceptance: The owner's username (without @) passes isValidBotUsername (T116) and is recorded where a reader looks for it: src/lib/bot/README.md 'Production status' and 'Going live' (the production bot's username; a username is public, not a secret), the example value in the NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME comment of .env.example, and docs/marketing/roommate-posts.md 'How to use a template' as the value to fill; nothing else changes in the repository (the owner sets the variable in Vercel and in his own .env.local)
The token of the production bot never appears in the repository, the progress entry or the chat (D76); the dev bot @passflatdev_bot and its token in .env.local are untouched

The progress entry reminds the owner of the steps that need the username: NEXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME in Vercel (the website's bot links render nothing until it is set), `npm run bot:posts` for the posting kit, `npm run bot:webhook` and `npm run bot:profile` with that bot's token
